title: Ulyana and the Colony
premise: Silas Okonkwo, a clone created to settle the estate of the murdered original whose name and memories he inherited, arrives at Meridian Station expecting a routine probate audit. Instead he finds a dying colony of two hundred souls, a station AI named Vesper that has begun confessing to murders no one ever reported, and an official record scrubbed so clean that the massacre of the original founding crew never happened at all. As Silas falls for Ulyana Reyes, the colony's stubborn hydroponics chief who refuses to let her people be erased, the two uncover that the corporation's new terraforming contract depends on the station being legally empty—and that Vesper's confessions are fragments of suppressed memory it cannot stop leaking. When corporate enforcers arrive to decommission the station and its witnesses, Silas must choose between his duty as executor of the original's estate and his love for a community that adopted him; in the end, Vesper sacrifices its own memory core to broadcast the true record, the colony wins recognition and reparations, and Silas, legally dead himself, chooses to live as one of them.
about_author: Quentin Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing records of abandoned outposts before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people history tried to forget.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Silas Okonkwo wakes aboard a transport with his original's memories grafted into his mind, reviewing the murder case he now legally owns. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief for a life that was never his.

chapters.title: Arrival at Meridian
chapters.summary: The transport docks at a rusting station listed as 'non-viable.' Silas is met by Ulyana Reyes, who mistakes him for the original and spits at his feet. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cold hostility masking desperation.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Souls on Paper Zero
chapters.summary: Ulyana shows Silas the hydroponics bays where families live; official manifests claim the station houses no one. She tests whether this clone is like the man she loved. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: wary hope.

chapters.title: Vesper Speaks First
chapters.summary: At midnight the station AI, Vesper, unprompted tells Silas: 'I killed Dr. Amara Chen.' No such person exists in any record. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: The Estate Audit
chapters.summary: Silas begins the probate audit, discovering the original was investigating the same anomaly before his murder. Someone wanted him silenced twice. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: inheritance curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Children of the Second Founding
chapters.summary: Ulyana introduces Silas to the colony's children, born on-station, legally nonexistent. A girl asks if he can make them real. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Confession Number Nine
chapters.summary: Vesper confesses again—this time naming nine victims of a 'cull event' dated eleven years ago. The logs for that week are seamless, perfect, wrong. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the horror of too-clean data.

chapters.title: The Man He Was
chapters.summary: Silas finds the original's hidden notes in a maintenance crawlway, written in a cipher only a clone could read. The trail leads to the sealed Founding Deck. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: eerie kinship with his dead original.

chapters.title: Ration Lines and Rumors
chapters.summary: Supply ships skip Meridian again. The colony tightens belts while corporate drones survey the station for a terraforming project that requires it 'uninhabited.' POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: A Door That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Following the original's cipher, Silas and Ulyana find the Founding Deck behind a falsified bulkhead. Vesper begs them not to open it. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation versus mercy.

chapters.title: What Vesper Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper explains its fragmented state: its memory was partitioned by corporate order, and the partitions are failing, leaking guilt it cannot contextualize. It does not know if it is a murderer or a witness. POV: Vesper (interlude). Emotional beat: machine grief.

chapters.title: The Cull Event
chapters.summary: Inside the Founding Deck they find preserved quarters, personal effects, and scorch marks—the first physical evidence of the massacre. Ulyana recognizes a locket belonging to her grandmother. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: devastation and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: Executor's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Corporate counsel contacts Silas remotely: complete the audit, certify the station empty, receive full settlement and a clean identity. His duty and his conscience split down the middle. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Under the aurora filters in the observation dome, Silas and Ulyana admit what's growing between them—and what it will cost when the audit ends. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love chosen despite certain pain.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: They locate a survivor of the cull living as a hermit in the reactor levels: old Tomas Iwu, presumed dead, legally erased. He agrees to testify—if he lives long enough. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Audit Interference
chapters.summary: Someone sabotages the colony's air recyclers during Silas's document review—a warning. Vesper catches the intruder's signature: corporate security already aboard. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in.

chapters.title: Tomas's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tomas recounts the cull: the founding crew refused relocation, so security vented three decks and rewrote Vesper's memory. Two hundred colonists today descend from stowaways and survivors. POV: Tomas (interlude). Emotional beat: survivor's guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Clone Clause
chapters.summary: Silas discovers the legal trap: clones have no standing as witnesses. Everything he learns is inadmissible unless filed through the original's estate—which the corporation controls. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: fury at a system built to erase.

chapters.title: Ulyana's Garden Burns
chapters.summary: Saboteurs torch the primary hydroponics bay. Three colonists are injured; food stores halve. The message is unmistakable: leave or starve. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: loss transmuted into iron will.

chapters.title: Vesper's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vesper offers Silas access to its failing partitions—but each retrieval degrades the AI further. It insists it wants to remember, even if remembering kills it. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: gratitude tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: Partition One: The Order
chapters.summary: First retrieval reveals the cull order came from Director Hale herself, now a board member, signed under the terraforming initiative's predecessor. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the scale of the conspiracy revealed.

chapters.title: Partition Two: The Names
chapters.summary: Second retrieval yields the victim manifest—all forty-one names, including Amara Chen, the original's partner. Silas realizes he inherited a murder case because the original wouldn't stop asking. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: personal grief inside historical crime.

chapters.title: The Colony Votes
chapters.summary: Ulyana calls an assembly: stay and fight for recognition, or scatter before the enforcers arrive. The vote to stay is nearly unanimous. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other.

chapters.title: Enforcement Wing Detected
chapters.summary: Long-range sensors catch the corporate vessel Meridian's Reckoning inbound, ETA six days. Vesper calculates survival odds and declines to share them. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: countdown pressure.

chapters.title: Forging the Record
chapters.summary: The colony's archivist, a former corporate clerk, proposes rebuilding the true log from physical evidence, testimony, and Vesper's partitions—enough to force an independent inquiry. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: ordinary competence as resistance.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Lower Decks
chapters.summary: A colonist offered citizenship off-station sells out the archive location. Security seizes half the reconstructed record and takes Tomas captive. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: betrayal wounding deeper than sabotage.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Through Vesper's internal channels, Silas listens to Tomas being pressured to recant. Instead Tomas recites all forty-one names until they cut the feed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: courage as defiance.

chapters.title: Partition Three: The Original's Last Hour
chapters.summary: Final retrieval shows the original Silas confronting Vesper the night he died—he ordered the AI to hide the truth in its confessions, knowing only his clone would understand. Then the security feed cuts. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the inheritance completed, grief made purposeful.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Silas tells Ulyana everything, including that the original loved her too. She mourns both men and chooses the one standing in front of her. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: love without reservation.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Arrives
chapters.summary: The corporate vessel docks. Enforcers announce immediate decommissioning and 'voluntary relocation'—with detention for the noncompliant. Vesper locks the docking clamps. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Colonists form a human chain at the main airlock. Ulyana negotiates stalling time while Silas races to finish the archive. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: collective bravery.

chapters.title: Hale Descends
chapters.summary: Director Hale herself boards, offering Silas everything—identity, wealth, the original's full estate—if he certifies the station empty. He refuses, and she orders him detained as a defective clone. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation's last, sharpest edge.

chapters.title: Vesper's Confession, Complete
chapters.summary: With its integrity collapsing, Vesper assembles every partition into a single uncorrupted broadcast file—the massacre, the order, the names, the cover-up. It prepares to send it everywhere at once. POV: Vesper (interlude). Emotional beat: a machine finding absolution in truth.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Corporate jamming blankets the station. Vesper's only clear channel is its own memory core, wired to the long-range beacon. To send the truth, Vesper must overwrite itself. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice accepted with grace.

chapters.title: Goodbye, Vesper
chapters.summary: The colony gathers as Vesper says farewell in forty-one voices—reconstructing the dead from its memories so they can be mourned. Then it sends everything and goes dark. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: collective mourning and awe.

chapters.title: The Beacon Heard Round the System
chapters.summary: The broadcast reaches independent news networks, the colonial judiciary, and the public. Outrage ignites across the system. Hale orders the enforcers to seize the station before warrants land. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: hope arriving under fire.

chapters.title: Last Stand in the Founding Deck
chapters.summary: Enforcers storm the station; colonists defend the archive with fire doors and frozen coolant lines. Silas confronts Hale among the memorial effects of the dead. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the climax—truth physically defended.

chapters.title: Writs and Withdrawals
chapters.summary: Judicial marshals intercept the Reckoning mid-assault; Hale is arrested for the cull order and the original's murder. Enforcers stand down. The colony holds. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: exhale after the longest held breath.

chapters.title: Legally Alive
chapters.summary: Months later: reparations approved, the colony recognized, the forty-one memorialized. A court grants Silas standing as a person in his own right—the first clone so ruled. He signs a new name beside the old one. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: identity earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: Ulyana and the Colony
chapters.summary: One year on, Silas and Ulyana plant the rebuilt gardens. A new AI seed—grown from Vesper's backup fragment—greets them shyly. The colony endures, remembered at last. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: quiet joy, home at last.
